definition: No main-thread heartbeat in any gated take of the macOS UI benchmark is delayed more than maximumAllowed milliseconds. The statistic is each take's maximumDelayedHeartbeatMS from MainThreadStallWatchdog (a 100 ms heartbeat, so a stall of D ms reads between D-100 and D), including the censored lower bound of any heartbeat still queued when the take ended (frontend heartbeatDelayDefinition completedAndCensoredPending). Gated takes are those scripts/check_macos_ui_bench.py stall_gate_applies selects: the floor tier always, every other Mac tier when it is the host's native tier.
basis: Maintainer decision 2026-09-25 (benchmark and telemetry audit #6). Replaces the zero-tolerance delayedHeartbeatCount50 gate, which 419 of 464 canonical M2 takes (90.3%) would have failed, with Apple's 250 ms hang threshold. 250 ms is not calibrated either: replayed on the same 464 takes (16 canonical mac-mini-m2-8gb runs, uiMaximumDelayedHeartbeatMS from completed heartbeats only, so before the censored lower bounds, which can only raise it), it fails 189 takes (40.7%) and all 16 runs (1 to 23 of 29 takes each); the four 2026-09-14 runs have 16 to 23 takes above it and per-run medians of 295-353 ms. The M6 runs another tier on faster hardware, so its distribution is unknown and the exploratory calibration run is planned as one expected to fail this gate: the checker prints every gated take's value (cell=value) to benchmark-gate.txt whether the run passes or fails, so a failing run still records the distribution. The limit stays provisional until one exploratory scripts/ui_test.sh macos benchmark on mac-mini-m6-16gb has recorded that distribution; the statistic and limit are then re-declared here with calibrationStatus calibrated and that run in calibrationRuns.
